featuresTitle: Built for watching in another language

explain.title: Mark it. Get it.
explain.sub: Machine translation gets the words, not always the meaning. Pause, mark the part of the translation you don't get, and Twinsub explains what the original says: the idiom, the field term, the cultural reference, the meme.
steps: Press ? next to the subtitles, or E. The video pauses.
Mark the confusing part of the translation.
Tap Explain. The answer appears under the line, in your language.
explain.tr: So we pivoted — honestly, we're basically the Uber for dog walking now.
explain.gist: An app that matches dog owners with walkers on demand, the way Uber matches riders with drivers. Said with a bit of self-mockery.
explain.background: "The Uber for X" was a stock startup pitch in the 2010s. It got used so much that saying it now sounds like a joke about yourself.
explain.quota: 5 free explanations a day. Pro: 1,000 a month for $4.99. Lifetime: $14.90 once, with your own API key. Dual subtitles are always free.
explain.orig: Así que pivotamos; sinceramente, ahora somos básicamente el Uber de pasear perros.

how.title: How to start
steps: Open any YouTube video that has subtitles, hand-made or auto-generated.
The first time you use a language pair, click the yellow prompt. Chrome downloads its translation pack in a few seconds.

faq.title: Questions
items: Yes. Dual subtitles are free and unlimited, with no account and no trial. Explanations are free 5 times a day.

Two. Twinsub Pro gives you 1,000 explanations a month instead of 5 a day, for $4.99 a month; cancel anytime from the Twinsub menu. Twinsub Lifetime is a one-time $14.90 that lets you use your own AI API key, for good. Dual subtitles stay free and unlimited either way.
Can I use my own API key?

Yes, with Twinsub Lifetime ($14.90 once) or while you have Pro. Pick OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq, xAI, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, Doubao, SiliconFlow or a local Ollama, or enter any base URL that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses or Claude Messages format. Your key is encrypted and stored only on your computer, and explanations go straight from Chrome to that provider, never through our server.
With the translator built into Chrome (Chrome 138 and newer). Each line is translated on your own computer in a few milliseconds, so nothing waits on a server.
Does it work with auto-generated subtitles?
Yes. Twinsub regroups YouTube's auto-generated captions into whole sentences before translating them, and follows whatever track you pick in the CC menu.
Which languages can I translate into?

39: English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Arabic, Hindi, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Thai, Turkish, Polish, Dutch, Ukrainian and more.

For subtitles, nothing. When you tap Explain, the words you marked and a few subtitle lines around them go to our server, which asks an AI model hosted in the United States for the answer. See the privacy policy.
Which browsers does it run on?
Chrome 138 or newer on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Other Chromium browsers can install it, but may not include Chrome's on-device translator.

pro.title: Thanks for going Pro
pro.ok: Twinsub Pro turns on within a few seconds. Go back to YouTube and keep watching.

pro.lifetimeOk: Your own API key is unlocked within a few seconds. Open the Twinsub menu, then AI settings, to add your provider and key.
pro.lifetimeCode: Your Lifetime code is in the AI settings. Enter it on your other computers, up to 5.
